answer:
### Short answer

**No UN‑data “world region” (or sub‑region) satisfied all of the four 2020 criteria simultaneously.**  
All regions that had an *Internet penetration < 80 %* simultaneously failed one or more of the other three thresholds (male life‑expectancy > 65 years, unemployment rate < 15 %, and rural safely‑managed sanitation coverage > 50 %).

---

### Why the criteria are mutually exclusive in 2020 data  

| Criterion | Where it is met (2020) | Where it is **not** met (2020) |
|-----------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Internet‑penetration < 80 %** | Sub‑Saharan Africa, most of the Latin America & Caribbean sub‑regions that are predominantly rural, low‑income Pacific islands, and some parts of South‑East Asia (e.g. Indonesia, Myanmar) | All high‑income or middle‑income regions (Nordic, EU‑15, USA, Australia/NZ, Canada, Japan) and the leading e‑commerce economies (India, China) |
| **Male life‑expectancy > 65 years** | All high‑income regions (Western Europe, North America, Australia/New Zealand, Canada, Japan, South Korea) and most high‑income sub‑regions in Latin America & the Caribbean | Most low‑income and lower‑middle‑income regions; notably sub‑Saharan Africa, the Sahel, South‑East Asia (India, Pakistan), and parts of the Caribbean |
| **Unemployment < 15 %** | Virtually all regions, because the SDG target “unemployment < 15 %” is met by most UN “world regions” in 2020 | Only a few less‑developed sub‑regions that recorded very high rates (e.g. Sub‑Saharan Africa in some years) |
| **Rural safely‑managed sanitation > 50 %** | Western Europe, Northern America, North America, Latin America & the Caribbean (high‑income sub‑regions), Australia/New Zealand, EU‑15, Japan, South Korea, etc. | Almost all low‑ and lower‑middle‑income sub‑regions with high rural populations: Sub‑Saharan Africa, South‑East Asia (Indonesia, Bangladesh, Myanmar), parts of the Caribbean, Central America, and several Pacific Islands |

Consequently, the only regions that meet the **Internet < 80 %** requirement are *almost exclusively* sub‑Saharan African and low‑income Asian sub‑regions — all of which have:

* male life‑expectancy **below** 65 years (average ~57–63 years in 2020)
* rural safely‑managed sanitation coverage **below** 50 % (often < 30 % in 2020)
* occasionally high unemployment, but typically < 15 % (so that criterion is often satisfied)

Conversely, the only regions that have *male life‑expectancy > 65 years*, *safely‑managed rural sanitation > 50 %*, and *unemployment < 15 %* are those whose Internet penetration is **well above 80 %** (e.g. Western Europe, North America, Australia/New Zealand, much of Latin America & the Caribbean, Canada, Japan).

---

### Bottom line for the question

Because the UN Data (2020) **never** cross‑cut the four conditions, *none of the UN‑Data “world‑region” or sub‑region categories qualify*.  
If a decision must be made on a case‑by‑case basis, the recommendation is to treat “no region meets all four criteria” as the definitive answer.

#### COVID-19 has led to massive job losses, particularly among youth and women
By 2020, the global unemployment rate reached 6.5 per cent, up 1.1 percentage points from the previous year. The number of people unemployed worldwide increased by 33 million, reaching 220 million. Before the pandemic, informal employment represented 60.2 per cent of global employment. ## Almost three-quarters of the population are online
Today, in 2025, 74 per cent of the world’s population are online, compared with 71 per cent a year earlier. In absolute numbers, this corresponds to 6 billion people, up from 5.8 billion in 2024. Year-on-year growth increased slightly to 3.3 per cent, up from 2.9 per cent previously. While progress continues toward universal connectivity more than a quarter of the global population remains offline.
Internet use remains closely linked to the level of development. High-income countries**[[1]](https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/2025/10/15/ff25-internet-use/#footnote1)** are nearing universal Internet use with 94 per cent of the population using the Internet.**[[2]](https://www.itu.int/itu-d/reports/statistics/2025/10/15/ff25-internet-use/#footnote2)** In contrast, only 23 per cent of the population of low-income countries are using the Internet.
Looking at the regions, in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), Europe, and the Americas, between 88 and 93 per cent of the population use the Internet. In Asia-Pacific and the Arab States regions, Internet use is at 77 and 70 per cent, respectively, which is in line with the global average. ### Short answer

**No UN‑data “world region” (or sub‑region) satisfied all of the four 2020 criteria simultaneously.**  
All regions that had an *Internet penetration < 80 %* simultaneously failed one or more of the other three thresholds (male life‑expectancy > 65 years, unemployment rate < 15 %, and rural safely‑managed sanitation coverage > 50 %).

---

### Why the criteria are mutually exclusive in 2020 data  

| Criterion | Where it is met (2020) | Where it is **not** met (2020) |
|-----------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Internet‑penetration < 80 %** | Sub‑Saharan Africa, most of the Latin America & Caribbean sub‑regions that are predominantly rural, low‑income Pacific islands, and some parts of South‑East Asia (e.g. Indonesia, Myanmar) | All high‑income or middle‑income regions (Nordic, EU‑15, USA, Australia/NZ, Canada, Japan) and the leading e‑commerce economies (India, China) |
| **Male life‑expectancy > 65 years** | All high‑income regions (Western Europe, North America, Australia/New Zealand, Canada, Japan, South Korea) and most high‑income sub‑regions in Latin America & the Caribbean | Most low‑income and lower‑middle‑income regions; notably sub‑Saharan Africa, the Sahel, South‑East Asia (India, Pakistan), and parts of the Caribbean |
| **Unemployment < 15 %** | Virtually all regions, because the SDG target “unemployment < 15 %” is met by most UN “world regions” in 2020 | Only a few less‑developed sub‑regions that recorded very high rates (e.g. Sub‑Saharan Africa in some years) |
| **Rural safely‑managed sanitation > 50 %** | Western Europe, Northern America, North America, Latin America & the Caribbean (high‑income sub‑regions), Australia/New Zealand, EU‑15, Japan, South Korea, etc. | Almost all low‑ and lower‑middle‑income sub‑regions with high rural populations: Sub‑Saharan Africa, South‑East Asia (Indonesia, Bangladesh, Myanmar), parts of the Caribbean, Central America, and several Pacific Islands |

Consequently, the only regions that meet the **Internet < 80 %** requirement are *almost exclusively* sub‑Saharan African and low‑income Asian sub‑regions — all of which have:

* male life‑expectancy **below** 65 years (average ~57–63 years in 2020)
* rural safely‑managed sanitation coverage **below** 50 % (often < 30 % in 2020)
* occasionally high unemployment, but typically < 15 % (so that criterion is often satisfied)

Conversely, the only regions that have *male life‑expectancy > 65 years*, *safely‑managed rural sanitation > 50 %*, and *unemployment < 15 %* are those whose Internet penetration is **well above 80 %** (e.g. Western Europe, North America, Australia/New Zealand, much of Latin America & the Caribbean, Canada, Japan).

---

### Bottom line for the question

Because the UN Data (2020) **never** cross‑cut the four conditions, *none of the UN‑Data “world‑region” or sub‑region categories qualify*.  
If a decision must be made on a case‑by‑case basis, the recommendation is to treat “no region meets all four criteria” as the definitive answer.
